- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 78–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “reversion to mean” after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates the downward trend in the latter half.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent strong downward momentum — e.g., after 75–80 peaks, it doesn’t sufficiently reduce forecasted values.
- Model shows lag in reacting to recent low prices — e.g., when true prices dip below 65, model doesn’t immediately reflect that in the forecast.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, leading to over-forecasted peaks that don’t materialize.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low prices — fails to recognize when prices are trending down from 70+.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecasts too high after recent highs, too low after recent lows, without sufficient adjustment.
- Model doesn’t account for seasonal or calendar-based patterns — e.g., consistent downward trend in last 10 days of forecast is not captured.
